raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` fails on XPU before it benchmarks the first config:
- It hard-codes CUDA: `torch.cuda.synchronize`, `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`, `torch.cuda.Event`, and a `"cuda"` cache-flush tensor.
- It uses Ray's global GPU id as the local device ordinal. Ray already isolates one card per worker, so on XPU that ordinal is out of range, as it is on ROCm.

The sibling `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py` already uses the device-generic APIs.

## Modifications

- `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`:
  - Synchronize, capture the graph and create events through `torch.get_device_module()`, with `torch.xpu.XPUGraph` on XPU.
  - Allocate the L2-flush buffer on the current device.
  - Seed through the device module.
  - Use device ordinal 0 on XPU, as on ROCm.
  - CUDA behavior is unchanged: every call resolves to `torch.cuda`.
- `README.md`: new "Intel XPU" section. Ray only registers Intel GPUs as `GPU` resources when `dpctl` is installed (it is part of the `ray` extra in `pyproject_xpu.toml`). Cards are selected with `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`.

## Accuracy Tests

Benchmark tooling only; no runtime code changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The tuner now runs end to end on Arc Pro B70; it was used to tune Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 for batch sizes 1-32.

For reference, those configs with `--moe-runner-backend triton` (4x B70, TP4, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 256 out, same tuned server flags as the default runner):

| | c=1 TPOT | c=1 TTFT | c=4 TPOT | c=16 TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Triton runner, default configs | 6.70 ms | 119 ms | 11.08 ms | 20.68 ms |
| Triton runner, B70-tuned configs | 6.62 ms | 37 ms | 25.84 ms | 23.30 ms |
| default XPU runner (sgl-kernel-xpu grouped GEMM) | 6.72 ms | 35 ms | 10.69 ms | 20.19 ms |

The tuned configs fix the Triton runner's prefill and help at c=1. They are worse at c>=4, and the default XPU runner is the better choice there, so this PR does not add config files. It only makes the tuner usable on XPU.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -145,6 +145,21 @@ python benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py \
     --tune
 ```
 
+#### Intel XPU
+
+Ray only registers Intel GPUs as `GPU` resources when `dpctl` is installed
+(`pip install dpctl`, also part of the `ray` extra in `pyproject_xpu.toml`).
+Select the cards to tune on with `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`; each Ray worker then sees
+its card as device 0:
+
+```bash
+ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=2 python benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
+    --tp-size 4 \
+    --batch-sizes 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
+    --tune
+```
+
 ### Configuration Files
 
 After tuning, configuration files will be generated:

@@ -203,35 +203,38 @@ def run():
                 block_shape=block_shape,
             )
 
+    device_module = torch.get_device_module()
+    graph_cls = torch.xpu.XPUGraph if _is_xpu else torch.cuda.CUDAGraph
+
     # JIT compilation & warmup
     run()
-    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    device_module.synchronize()
 
-    # Capture 10 invocations with CUDA graph
-    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
-    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+    # Capture 10 invocations with a device graph
+    graph = graph_cls()
+    with device_module.graph(graph):
         for _ in range(10):
             run()
-    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    device_module.synchronize()
 
     # Warmup
     for _ in range(5):
         graph.replay()
-    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    device_module.synchronize()
 
     # Flush L2 cache with 256 MB data
-    cache_flush = torch.empty(int(256e6 // 4), dtype=torch.int, device="cuda")
+    cache_flush = torch.empty(int(256e6 // 4), dtype=torch.int, device=get_device())
     cache_flush.zero_()
 
-    start_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(num_iters)]
-    end_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(num_iters)]
+    start_events = [device_module.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(num_iters)]
+    end_events = [device_module.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(num_iters)]
 
     for i in range(num_iters):
         prepare(i)
         start_events[i].record()
         graph.replay()
         end_events[i].record()
-    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    device_module.synchronize()
 
     latencies: List[float] = []
     for i in range(num_iters):
@@ -250,8 +253,9 @@ def __init__(self, seed: int, server_args: ServerArgs) -> None:
         # Get the device ID to allocate tensors and kernels
         # on the respective GPU. Ray isolates each worker to a single visible
         # GPU via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, so the local ordinal is always 0. On
-        # ROCm using the global ray gpu id here raises "invalid device ordinal".
-        self.device_id = 0 if is_hip() else int(ray.get_gpu_ids()[0])
+        # ROCm and XPU using the global ray gpu id here raises an out-of-range
+        # device ordinal.
+        self.device_id = 0 if (is_hip() or _is_xpu) else int(ray.get_gpu_ids()[0])
         set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(server_args)
 
     def benchmark(
